tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the App Router entry files to see that this is a small Next.js frontend named my-app, with a root layout, a minimal home page, global providers, fonts, and metadata forming the application base.
tour.languageLesson: In a Next.js App Router project, layout.tsx defines persistent UI and providers, while page.tsx defines the route content.

tour.title: App Shell and Routes
tour.description: Follow the root and auth layouts into the route group to understand how pages are nested, how the auth section gets its own wrapper, and where the sign-in route currently lives.

tour.title: Authentication Sign-In Feature
tour.description: Read the sign-in page together with AuthForm to see the intended authentication surface: a route page backed by a client-side form using React Hook Form, Zod validation, shared fields, and disabled submit state handling.
tour.languageLesson: Client form components in App Router code usually declare client behavior separately from server-rendered route files.

tour.title: UI Primitives
tour.description: Explore the low-level shadcn-style primitives that compose navigation, buttons, fields, inputs, feedback, selections, separators, textareas, and tooltips across the app.

tour.title: Shared Form Wrappers
tour.description: Move from primitives to the React Hook Form wrappers that standardize labels, descriptions, validation errors, disabled states, and control-specific behavior for text, password, select, checkbox, and textarea inputs.
tour.languageLesson: Typed form wrappers reduce repetition by centralizing registration, controlled values, and error display around reusable UI primitives.

tour.title: API, Runtime, Styling, and Configuration
tour.description: Finish with the cross-cutting pieces: Axios setup, typed API helpers, TanStack Query defaults, error normalization, class-name merging, global Tailwind tokens, and the project configuration and analysis files that shape development.
